_comment: Single source of truth for browser-capture connector identity (#61 Phase 2 / steering point 1). Read directly by the Rust connector host (src-tauri/src/bin/callosum_connector.rs via include_str!), the NSIS installer hook generator (packaging/generate_connector_nsh.py), the extension's dev-build tooling, and tests/test_connector_identity.py. Nothing hardcodes these strings a second time.
_production_extension_ids_comment: Deliberately EMPTY. Neither the Chrome Web Store nor Microsoft Edge Add-ons has ever assigned this extension a real ID -- it has not been published to either store yet. Do NOT fill this in with a guessed or arbitrary ID: Chrome ignores a manifest 'key' field on a NEW Web Store item and assigns its own ID at first publish, so there is no way to know the real ID before that happens. An empty allowed_origins list is the honest, SAFE state: the installer still writes a fully-formed, valid native-messaging manifest, so the plumbing (registry write/remove, ownership checks, /UPDATE guard) is verifiable now -- it just allows no caller yet, which is correct for an unpublished extension. When Chrome Web Store and/or Edge Add-ons assign real IDs, add them here (they may differ between the two stores; both are supported since this is a list) and ship that as an ordinary app update -- the installer hook re-writes this manifest on every install/update from whatever is configured at build time.
_dev_extension_comment: A REAL RSA-2048 public key, generated once for this project so 'Load unpacked' produces the SAME 32-character extension ID on every machine and in CI -- Chrome's unpacked-ID derivation otherwise hashes the extension's absolute filesystem path, which differs per checkout. The private key was discarded immediately after deriving this ID: 'Load unpacked' only ever reads manifest.json's 'key' field (the public key), nothing signs with the private half locally. This ID is registered ONLY under dev_native_host_name by tools/run_dev.py, gated behind CALLOSUM_CONNECTOR_ALLOW_DEV_BUILD=1, and is NEVER shipped or added to production_extension_ids.
distribution_model: Chrome Web Store and Microsoft Edge Add-ons are two separate store submissions (separate developer accounts, separate review pipelines) sharing ONE production manifest.json. If a future publish pins the same manifest 'key' for both packages, both stores can be made to honor the same derived ID, which is why production_extension_ids is a LIST rather than a single string -- but do not assume that happens automatically; each store's assigned ID must be confirmed after that store's own first publish and added here explicitly.
